rationale: Both replace the character-by-character state machine with the same line-based design: apply emphasis first, then classify each line, using strings.Builder, so both are big improvements. A is tighter and more precise. headerLevel returns (level, ok) and requires 1-6 '#' characters followed by a space, and list items require '* '. That matches markdown semantics and makes each classification a single check. B splits the logic into several small helpers but computes headerLevel up to twice per line. Its rules are looser: '*foo' counts as a list item and '#foo' as a header. It also checks isListItem twice in the loop. A's refactoring notes are more informative too, for example the explicit warning that emphasis replacement only applies to the first pair in the whole document. B's decomposition is readable, but A is simpler, avoids redundant work and is more robust on edge cases.
